## 1. Scope

Covers WP1 sample tracking from field collection at Pallasjärvi through extraction, sequencing, and analysis-ready metadata — designed to stay compatible with WP2 (Grimsö) metadata so the two work packages can eventually be merged for cross-site comparison.

WP1 is single-site and prospective: every sample comes from the September 2026 Pallasjärvi campaign, and there is no archived-sample component. This is the main respect in which the design departs from the original proposal, and it is why connectivity has to be defined from within-campaign data (§2).

## 2. Connectivity definition (operational)

Since there's no multi-year history to select connected/unconnected dyads from, connectivity for WP1 must be defined from within-campaign data:

::: {.callout-important}

**PLACEHOLDER** — exact operational definition, e.g. co-capture in the same small quadrat within the two-night session vs. capture in different groups or habitats. This determines what counts as a "connected" vs. "unconnected" dyad in the eventual model. The finest available host scale is the 15 × 15 m quadrat: animals are recorded to quadrat only, not to a trap or corner, so any definition based on trap-station or burrow co-capture is not observable (fieldwork protocol §2).

:::

## 3. Sample ID scheme

::: {.callout-note}

**In use since 14 Sep 2026** — see fieldwork protocol §7, which is authoritative.

- Soil: SQ number + corner letter, e.g. `31A`. Unique because each corner is sampled once.
- Field blanks: SQ number alone, e.g. `31`; always opened at corner A.
- Reference soils: `REF-F1`…`REF-F4`, `REF-P1`…`REF-P4`.
- Gut: Henttonen's animal ID plus tissue, assigned at transfer to cryovials in Uppsala; the field record carries `caecum_sample_id` and `colon_sample_id` per animal.

`sample_id` in the data is the tube label verbatim. A `PAL-` prefix is added only when WP1 and WP2 tables are merged.

:::

## 4. Metadata schema

Field-stage metadata are the two transcribed tables defined in the fieldwork protocol §8 (`wp1_soil_log`, `wp1_voles`; templates in `data-capture/`). Their shared keys are `collection_date`, `habitat`, and the sampling unit: `sq_id` for quadrats or `line_id` for pitfall lines. Group is not recorded in the field; it is derived from the corner coordinates and attached afterwards (fieldwork protocol §2). The soil log additionally carries `corner` and `depth_cm`; corner coordinates are a separate table (`wp1_corner_coords`), one row per corner, joined on `sq_id` + `corner`; the vole table carries Henttonen's `animal_id`, which joins to his morphometrics (species, sex, age class, mass) and to the PUUV result.

Not captured, because the trapping design does not record them: trap station within quadrat, burrow identity, and trap-to-burrow distance. Animals are resolved to the small quadrat only. Trap night is recoverable from `collection_date`.

Lab-stage fields, added per sample as processing proceeds:

| Field | Captured by |
|---|---|
| storage_medium (frozen, no preservative, for all field samples) | Field team |
| extraction_batch_id | Lab |
| extraction_date | Lab |
| extraction_kit_lot | Lab |
| pcr_batch_id | Lab |
| sequencing_run_id | Lab / NGI |

## 5. Batch design

To avoid confounding batch effects with the biological variable of interest:

- Extraction and library-prep batches should be **blocked across grids**, not run grid-by-grid in sequence
- Once the connectivity definition (§2) is settled, batches should also be blocked across connectivity status, so "connected" and "unconnected" individuals aren't systematically processed in different runs
- Field blanks and off-grid soil controls should appear in every batch, not be run separately at the end

::: {.callout-note}

**PLACEHOLDER** — actual randomization scheme once N and grid count are known; a simple stratified-random assignment to batches is probably sufficient, but worth deciding the block size against expected batch capacity (how many
samples per extraction/PCR run).

:::
